published_statement: F&T (5.1)-(5.2): on ds^2 = -dt^2 + a^2[dchi^2 + sinh^2 chi dOmega^2] the mode functions of a scalar field of mass mu have omega_q = sqrt((q^2+1)/a^2 + mu^2), 0<q<oo. (5.6): 'Both (3.2) and (5.5) can, in fact, be written as  -(1/4pi^3) INT_0^oo dw INT_C^oo dw' w'^2 sqrt(w'^2-C^2) |(f^1/2)^(w+w')|^2 = -(1/16pi^3) INT_C^oo du |(f^1/2)^(u)|^2 u^4 Q_3(u/C)', (5.7): 'C = sqrt(kappa/a^2 + mu^2), kappa = 0 Minkowski space, 1 open universe'. 'Since Q_3(x) is an increasing function on [1,oo), the bound for general a is tighter than that in Minkowski space for all sampling functions f(t).' (3.5): Q_n(x) = (n+1) x^-(n+1) INT_1^x dy y^2 (y^2-1)^(n/2-1). Massless (mu=0), open universe: C = 1/a.
published_hypotheses: (2.1)-(2.2): globally static (n+1)-dim spacetime, timelike Killing vector d_t; free real scalar field of mass mu >= 0 obeying (1/|g_tt|) d_t^2 phi - grad_i grad^i phi + mu^2 phi = 0 -- MINIMAL coupling, no xi R term (p.3)
a complete orthonormal set of positive-frequency modes exists (p.3)
the bound is on the NORMAL-ORDERED energy density, in the Fock space built on the static vacuum, measured by static observers (p.3)
sampling function f smooth, non-negative, sufficiently rapid decay; not necessarily even (p.3)
Sec. 5: ultrastatic open RW, spatial section H^3 with scale a constant (5.1); modes and sum rule (5.3)-(5.4) taken from ref. [18] (Parker-Fulling)
C in (5.6)-(5.7) is the minimum mode frequency omega_min (cf. (2.13) 'omega_min = min omega_lambda'), in frequency units
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (named nowhere at the use site): MINIMAL COUPLING xi = 0. fewsterteo.py:73-78 and witness_gap() fewsterteo.py:202-211 (canonical hypotheses: 'ultrastatic open RW ...', 'massless field' only). F&T (2.2) is minimally coupled and (5.2)'s (q^2+1)/a^2 is the minimal spectrum. Computed here: R(R x H^3_a) = -6/a^2, so C(xi) = sqrt((1-6xi)/a^2 + mu^2); conformal coupling xi = 1/6 gives C = 0 on the SAME H^3 witness. The value 1/a_c is a property of xi = 0, not of H^3. (fewsterteo.py:116 names minimal coupling, but for Fewster & Smith, not for the F&T witness.) Direction: xi > 0 shrinks C and so the witness tightening -- it would only strengthen the refusal of 72.599/72.247, never move it in M's favour; xi < 0 would enlarge C.

WORDING (a discrepancy, not an error in any number): fewsterteo.py:77 'the spectral gap 1/a_c' and the canonical name 'Spectral gap of the Laplacian on H^3 ... equals 1/a_c'. Computed here: the bottom of the spectrum of -Delta on H^3(a) is 1/a^2 (eigenvalue units, = McKean's (n-1)^2/(4a^2) at n=3); 1/a is its square root, the minimum FREQUENCY omega_min, which is exactly F&T's C. The tree uses C in frequency units (c/b), so every figure is F&T's C; only the name 'spectral gap of the Laplacian = 1/a_c' is dimensionally off. Also: the bottom is the infimum of a purely continuous spectrum (q -> 0 mode chi/sinh chi is not L^2), not an isolated eigenvalue.

NOT NAMED at the use site: F&T's state class and normalisation -- the bound constrains the normal-ordered energy density relative to the static vacuum in its Fock space (F&T p.3). fewsterteo.py:73-78 compares F&T bounds to each other (the ratio), where the static-vacuum offset does not enter; it is recorded, not shown to move anything here.

NOT EXAMINED here (belongs to the C_F / sampler audit): F&T assume f smooth; the tree's sampler is the clamped-beam fundamental (fewsterteo.py:224-230), g = f^1/2 C^1 with compact support. The key's claim (C = 1/a_c) does not depend on the sampler.

EXTRAPOLATED beyond F&T's class (does not touch the refused figures): fewsterteo.py:98-100 and cavity_gap() fewsterteo.py:214-217 feed a cavity gap C = b/R_s into (5.6)'s Q_3 form. F&T derive that form for the Minkowski-massive (C = mu) and open-RW (q^2 density of states) spectra only; ratio(C) is exact for H^3 of radius 1/C or Minkowski with mu = C, but a cavity has a discrete spectrum and another density of states. The 'ratio 0.999999' at the cavity is therefore an illustration, not an F&T evaluation. The refusal itself rests on GAP_HYPOTHESIS (fewsterteo.py:175-176, C = 0), which the tree names.

ADDED (correct): the tree matches a_c to the corridor's demand through 3c^4/(8 pi G a_c^2) = |rho| (fewsterteo.py:205-210). F&T treat R x H^3 as a background with no field equation for a. Computed here: G_tt of the ultrastatic open RW is -3/a^2, so rho = -3c^4/(8 pi G a^2) < 0 and the matching of |rho| is right.

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Osterbrink, arXiv:0708.2450 (2007), 'Quantum Energy Inequalities for the Non-Minimally Coupled Scalar Field'
later_literature.what: Abstract: for xi != 0 local energy-density averages are 'unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states', in contrast with the minimally coupled field's state-independent QEI; only a state-dependent QEI holds for 0 < xi <= 1/4. So minimal coupling is not merely what fixes C = 1/a -- it is the hypothesis under which an F&T-type state-independent bound exists at all. Confirms that the dropped hypothesis is load-bearing.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: F&T (5.6)-(5.7) is a THEOREM about a spectrum, not an extrapolation from data; its conclusion C = sqrt(1/a^2 + mu^2) depends on no measured number, and the eigenvalue (q^2+1)/a^2 was re-derived here from the paper's own mode functions. The only numerical input on the tree's side, C_w = 25 sqrt 2, depends on the tree's own design parameters (M_OVER_B, A_OVER_B), with G and c cancelling identically. What was not 'lacked data' but known in 1999 and simply left unnamed by the tree is the coupling: F&T assumed minimal coupling; the 2007 result of Fewster & Osterbrink (data the 1999 authors did not have) shows that for xi != 0 no state-independent bound of this type exists. That later knowledge does not change F&T's conclusion (their xi = 0 statement stands); it narrows the class the tree may transplant it to. Evidence either way: no datum moved; no later result contradicts (5.7) at xi = 0.
grade_evidence: The number is right: C = omega_min = 1/a_c for a massless MINIMALLY coupled field on ultrastatic R x H^3_a, re-derived symbolically from F&T's own modes (5.2)-(5.3) and (5.7), and C_w = 25 sqrt 2 = 35.35533905932738 re-derived with G and c cancelling. It is NARROWED only in hypothesis, per the rubric's 'a hypothesis the tree drops': (i) the tree's use site (fewsterteo.py:73-78, 202-211) names 'massless' but not minimal coupling, and C(xi) = sqrt((1-6xi)/a_c^2) computed here shows 1/a_c holds at xi = 0 only (conformal coupling gives C = 0 on the same witness); Fewster & Osterbrink 0708.2450 shows no state-independent bound of this type survives xi != 0. (ii) Wording: 'spectral gap of the Laplacian = 1/a_c' is dimensionally a frequency gap -- the Laplacian's bottom is 1/a_c^2 -- a discrepancy in the name, not in any figure. Neither point moves the refused figures 72.599/72.247 in M's favour: xi > 0 only shrinks the witness tightening, and the refusal rests on the separately named GAP_HYPOTHESIS (C = 0 for an asymptotically flat corridor). Not WRONG: nothing contradicts F&T or the tree's number.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the use site names 'minimally coupled (xi = 0)' beside 'massless' and calls C the minimum frequency omega_min = sqrt(lambda_0) (lambda_0 = 1/a_c^2), matching F&T (2.2)/(5.7). To WRONG: a computed eigenvalue of the H^3 Laplacian below 1/a^2 on L^2, or a reading of F&T (5.7) with C != sqrt(kappa/a^2 + mu^2) -- neither found; the script's control shows the check can fail (conformal coupling returns 0).
